newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds steady, US data narrows spread vs Bund.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds steady, US data narrows spread vs Bund.

text.p: Irish bond prices were steady in strong turnover on Tuesday, while spreads against Germany closed in slightly on the back of market-friendly U.S. retail sales figures, dealers said.

"We saw some profit-taking after the U.S. figures came out, despite the fact that they were market-friendly," one dealer said. "There are plenty of numbers still to come this week and I think people just thought they'd bag a bit of profit on today's new highs."

By 1510 GMT, the Irish 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 12 pence from Monday's close at 102.35 to yield 5.79 percent, while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was down three pence from the close at 109.67 to yield 6.46 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds had narrowed their spread over German bunds and were trading 123 basis points above in the five-year area and 90 basis points over Germany in the 10-year area.
Trading, largely matched, had been at a strong level throughout the day, the dealer added, but mainly within range. Price movements were called modest.
U.S. April retail sales showed a drop of 0.3 percent, in line with most forecasts, helping to cool recent concern over the imminence of an aggressive rates hike by the Federal reserve.
The Treasury note/Bund gap squeezed in two basis points on the news.

Elsewhere the UK gilt/Bund gap slimmed one basis point after widening earlier as the Bank of England's monthly inflation report said futher moderate policy tightening was needed to meet a 2.5 percent inflation target.
Looking ahead, dealers said, the market would continue to focus on inflation-indicative data, including U.S. CPI and jobless figures, and the Philadelphia Fed Survey later in the week.
The National Treasury Management Agency is due to announce the amount and maturity date of stock to be auctioned on May 20.
Dealers said they expected the stock to be short-end, most likely five-year bonds.
